name: centers crops with floor origins while preserving channels and dtype
input: a five-by-six RGB uint8 image cropped to three-by-three
test:
import numpy as np
image = np.arange(5 * 6 * 3, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(5, 6, 3)
before = image.copy()
actual = center_crop(image, 3, 3)
assert actual.dtype == np.uint8
assert np.array_equal(actual, image[1:4, 1:4, :])
assert np.array_equal(image, before)

name: uses the supplied RNG for crop and white-canvas placement
input: a grayscale four-by-five integer image with a seeded generator
test:
import numpy as np
image = np.arange(20, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(4, 5)
seed = 17
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
actual_crop = random_crop(image, 2, 3, rng)
expected_rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
top = expected_rng.integers(4 - 2 + 1)
left = expected_rng.integers(5 - 3 + 1)
assert np.array_equal(actual_crop, image[top:top + 2, left:left + 3])
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
actual_canvas = random_crop_paste_on_white(image, 2, 3, rng)
expected_rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
crop_top = expected_rng.integers(3)
crop_left = expected_rng.integers(3)
paste_top = expected_rng.integers(3)
paste_left = expected_rng.integers(3)
expected = np.full_like(image, np.iinfo(image.dtype).max)
expected[paste_top:paste_top + 2, paste_left:paste_left + 3] = image[crop_top:crop_top + 2, crop_left:crop_left + 3]
assert np.array_equal(actual_canvas, expected)

name: preserves float RGBA pixels and fills every untouched channel with white
input: an asymmetric float RGBA image with a seeded crop and paste
test:
import numpy as np
image = np.arange(3 * 5 * 4, dtype=np.float32).reshape(3, 5, 4) / 100
before = image.copy()
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
actual = random_crop_paste_on_white(image, 1, 2, rng)
oracle_rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
ct, cl = int(oracle_rng.integers(3)), int(oracle_rng.integers(4))
pt, pl = int(oracle_rng.integers(3)), int(oracle_rng.integers(4))
# Construct the expected canvas one pixel at a time, independently of slicing/paste.
expected = np.ones(image.shape, dtype=np.float32)
for dy in range(1):
    for dx in range(2):
        expected[pt + dy, pl + dx] = before[ct + dy, cl + dx]
assert actual.shape == image.shape and actual.dtype == image.dtype
assert np.array_equal(actual, expected)
assert np.array_equal(image, before)

name: full-size and single-pixel crops remain valid for integer and single-channel images
input: a signed integer 1x1 image and a full-size 2x3x1 image
test:
import numpy as np
for image in (np.array([[-3]], dtype=np.int16), np.arange(6, dtype=np.uint16).reshape(2, 3, 1)):
    h, w = image.shape[:2]
    before = image.copy()
    for actual in (center_crop(image, h, w),
                   random_crop(image, h, w, np.random.default_rng(4)),
                   random_crop_paste_on_white(image, h, w, np.random.default_rng(4))):
        assert actual.shape == image.shape and actual.dtype == image.dtype
        assert np.array_equal(actual, before)
    assert np.array_equal(image, before)
